Cooperative Transport of Unknown Objects by Distributed Effort Regulation in Multi-agent Systems
radar.summary: A distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy is proposed for objects of unknown shape, size, geometry, mass and mass distribution without any prior knowledge about the object or number of robots involved in the transportation process. Robots follow the boundary of the object and dynamically determine viable pushing points. A novel object-model-free heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation method is proposed to promote goal-directed object motion; robots regulate their pushing effort using individual and collective heading errors. Robots dynamically relocate around the object boundary if a pushing point is lost or the required pushing effort exceeds its capability to correct its heading. The proposed method is validated using simple and complex shapes with convex and non-convex boundary regions and dynamically changing weight distribution of objects. Detailed analysis on the effects of robot distribution and initial object pose on the transportation performance in terms of required time and path efficiency is also presented. Scalability analysis revealed that object transportation time is dependent on the number of pushing surfaces available which in turn depends on the object size, shape, and set inter-robot safety distance. The proposed system yielded highly efficient object paths with consistent elapsed transport times over several trials robust to external disturbances such as non-uniform friction between contacting surfaces and robot wheel slip.
radar.summary_short: A distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy is proposed for objects of unknown shape, size, geometry, mass and mass distribution without any prior knowledge about the object or number of robots involved in the transportation process.

radar.title: Simple and Effective: A Deterministic Auction with Support Information
radar.summary: We study an auction design problem where a seller aims to sell a single item to multiple bidders with independent private values. The seller knows only an upper bound on these values and does not know their distribution. The objective is to devise a deterministic auction mechanism effective across a broad set of distributions. We propose a second price auction with a reserve price set at half of the upper bound. Even though no deterministic mechanism can achieve a positive fraction of the maximum achievable expected revenue across all distributions, we show that our mechanism achieves at least [Formula: see text] ([Formula: see text] under independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) values) of the maximum expected revenue for a broad range of distributions of practical importance, where [Formula: see text] depends on the number of bidders and takes values in [Formula: see text]. Numerical experiments under randomly generated distributions demonstrate the superior performance of our mechanism in the vast majority of the generated instances compared to benchmark mechanisms from the literature. We also account for errors in the upper bound estimate. History: This paper has been accepted for the Mathematics of Operations Research Special Issue on Market Design.

radar.title: Maintaining Coordination in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Under Pairwise Asynchronous Link Failures Through Cached-Message Reuse
radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) relies on communication when local observations are incomplete. Pairwise asynchronous link failures interrupt different directed links at different times and remove part of the information used for coordination. This paper studies whether agents can maintain coordination by reusing the latest message received from each unavailable neighbor. We propose Temporal Graph-based Neighbor Aggregation with Age-Penalized Communication (TGN-APC). Each agent stores one message per neighbor and limits reuse by message age. TGN-APC reuses a valid cached message and subtracts an age penalty from its attention score. We evaluate the method on the Vectorized Multi-Agent Simulator Navigation task with ten independent training seeds. Cache reuse significantly improves return and team completion over direct one-hop communication under short and long failure bursts. An age penalty coefficient of 0.10 does not significantly improve on cache reuse without an age term. Matched validation-based coefficient selection shows no significant difference between score penalization and exponential content scaling after multiple-testing correction. A two-hop current-message variant gives the highest long-burst return, but it uses about 83% more active transmissions than TGN-APC. These results support cached-message reuse for the tested task and failure model. They do not establish a separate performance gain from the selected age penalty.
radar.summary_short: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) relies on communication when local observations are incomplete. Pairwise asynchronous link failures interrupt different directed links at different times and remove part of the information used for coordination.

radar.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) supports coordinated decision-making in distributed Web services, multi-robot control, and collaborative games through learned coordination conventions. When deployment requirements change, a previously useful convention may become obsolete or unsafe. For example, revised cache-sharing permissions in Web content delivery may require caches to abandon a learned division of storage and serving roles while maintaining efficient delivery. Teams must therefore remove the specified convention while preserving useful cooperation. This is challenging because the same relational pattern can be reproduced by different agents across different histories. Runtime shielding leaves the underlying coordination preference intact and can impair task progress, while existing reinforcement unlearning and trajectory-deletion methods do not directly target role-invariant conventions. This paper formalizes this problem as semantic coordination-strategy unlearning and proposes CARVE.CARVE uses causal coordination attribution to identify influential interactions and retain-aware subspace updates to limit interference with unrelated behaviors. Counterfactual re-coordination helps agents learn productive alternatives, while adversarial auditing tests whether the target convention can still be recovered. Accepted updates are merged into decentralized actors for direct deployment. Evaluation across five cooperative MARL benchmarks shows that CARVE reduces mean nominal convention-completion and worst-case elicitation rates by 91.4\% and 83.3\%, respectively.The median utility loss is 5.9\%, and measured inference latency matches that of the original policies.
radar.summary_short: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) supports coordinated decision-making in distributed Web services, multi-robot control, and collaborative games through learned coordination conventions.

radar.title: Learning to Clear Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets
radar.summary: Peer-to-peer energy markets are a promising paradigm for integrating distributed energy resources. A large body of work models their clearing as distributed optimization or generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems which let prosumers coordinate trades and local resources without a central operator. Yet, the computational and communication burden of distributed optimization and GNE-seeking algorithms poses a major challenge to deployment at scale. We propose a learning-to-optimize framework for decentralized markets that uses historical data to accelerate clearing algorithms without additional communication. To enforce convergence by design, we train summable augmentations to a baseline algorithm, using graph neural networks to learn permutation-equivariant updates for markets of varying size and topology. We instantiate the framework for computing a variational GNE in the market model of Le Cadre et al. (2020) with a distributed Douglas-Rachford algorithm, but the idea extends to other models and base algorithms. Numerical experiments show improved convergence and illustrate the robustness of our method to out-of-distribution instances.
